name: p4-0408-drain-node-path
title: One node's drain, change, validate, return path
spec: 1600-wide SVG, flow left to right for one GPU node. Boxes: Drain from Slurm (scontrol update State=DRAIN, delegate_to the Slurm controller), Wait until no jobs remain (squeue -h -w, until stdout is empty, retries 120, delay 30), block: apply_changes then Validate, Return to service (scontrol update State=RESUME). From the block a rescue arrow goes down to a box: fail with message, node left DRAINED for investigation. Note under the rescue box: no always resume on purpose, only a healthy node returns to service. Orange only on the rescue box. No crossing arrows.
alt: A flow showing one node drained, waited empty, changed and validated, then resumed, with a failure path that leaves the node drained.
cap: The failure path leaves the node drained, and only full success reaches the resume step.

name: p4-0408-handler-vs-state-check
title: Handler memory versus a state check
spec: 1600-wide SVG, two columns. Left column Handler says: something changed so restart; steps config task changed, notify queued, a later task fails, handler never runs, service stays stale. Right column State check says: the running thing must match the thing on disk; steps systemctl show -p ActiveEnterTimestampMonotonic dcgm-exporter, register started, changed_when false, compare with config mtime from stat, restart if process started before the file was written. Bottom line: the second statement stays true even after a failure wipes out the first. Orange on the right column header.
alt: Two columns comparing a handler notification that can be lost after a failure with a state check that compares process start time to config file time.
cap: A state check stays true after a failure that would erase a handler's notification.

name: p4-0408-meta-exits
title: Planned exits versus failures
spec: 1600-wide SVG table-like comparison of four controls from the chapter: meta end_host (stop this host, no failure, when skip_this_host), meta end_play (end the play for everyone, not a failure, when dry_run_only), meta clear_host_errors (resets failed hosts, rare, hides the reason), fail (explicit stop, msg Refusing to run in production without change ticket, when env is prod and no change_ticket). Group the first two plus end_batch under a heading Clean planned exit, fail under Explicit stop, clear_host_errors under Use rarely. Orange on fail row only.
anchor: ### Stopping the play and fleet-level policies
alt: A grouped comparison of meta end_host, end_play, clear_host_errors and fail showing which are clean exits and which stop the run.
cap: Meta exits are planned and clean, fail is an explicit stop, and clearing host errors hides the reason for a failure.

name: p4-0408-when-string-trap
title: The string false trap in when
spec: 1600-wide SVG, two lanes. Lane one: run with -e flag=false, the value arrives as the string false, when: flag treats a non-empty string as true, task runs when it should skip. Lane two: fix with when: flag | bool, string false becomes boolean false, task skips. Footer: write the bare expression when: var, not when: "{{ var }}". Orange on the fix lane.
alt: Two lanes showing a string false passed with -e being treated as true and the bool filter fixing it.
cap: The bool filter turns the string false into a real false so the condition evaluates as intended.

name: p4-0408-control-flow-symptoms
title: Control-flow symptom to fix ladder
spec: 1600-wide SVG, three-column ladder rows of Symptom, Likely cause, Fix using the debugging table: Handler never ran (task not changed, earlier failure, name typo; -v, force_handlers, flush_handlers); Handler ran every time (task not idempotent; fix the source of changes); Task skipped unexpectedly (when false, string vs bool; -vv shows false_condition); rescue ran but play is green (rescue handled it; re-raise with fail, check rescued count); Loop result weird (register gives results list; map); Retries did not stop (until never true; print register with -v); Included tasks not tagged (dynamic include; import_tasks or apply). Orange on the -vv false_condition fix.
alt: A table of control-flow symptoms with their likely causes and fixes.
cap: Start from the symptom, check the likely cause, and use -vv or the debug strategy to see which branch ran.
